 Poste d’étudiant(e) ou de nouveau diplômé(e) d’EDC – Équipe de soutien aux ventes (hiver 2027) 
 À propos d’EDC : À Exportation et développement Canada (EDC), nous aidons les entreprises canadiennes à réussir à l’étranger. En tant que société d’État à vocation financière, EDC propose des solutions financières innovantes et des conseils d’experts pour aider les entreprises à explorer de nouveaux marchés, à atténuer leurs risques et à se développer.
 Pourquoi vous joindre à EDC? 
 Collaborez avec une équipe diversifiée et expérimentée.
 Épanouissez-vous dans un environnement axé sur le soutien et le travail d’équipe.
 Influencez les communautés à l’échelle mondiale en stimulant la croissance durable des marchés émergents.
 Travaillez dans une entreprise reconnue comme l’un des 100 meilleurs employeurs du Canada, l’un des meilleurs employeurs pour la diversité au Canada et l’un des employeurs canadiens favorisant le plus la conciliation travail-famille.
 Profitez d’un programme d’avantages globaux comprenant des avantages sociaux, des congés, des programmes de bien-être et des occasions de perfectionnement professionnel.
 Aperçu de l’équipe et du poste 
 L’Équipe de la facilitation des ventes fournit à nos professionnels de la vente les outils, la formation, les communications et les renseignements nécessaires à leur réussite. Nous recherchons une étudiante ou un étudiant fiable capable d’effectuer du travail rigoureux et conforme à l’image de marque, de bien gérer ses priorités et d’apporter un soutien proactif à l’équipe. La personne choisie doit également être organisée et soucieuse du détail.
 Principales responsabilités 
 Mettre à jour et vérifier la qualité du matériel de formation, des présentations, des communications et des documents afin d’en garantir l’exactitude, la cohérence et l’accessibilité et de s’assurer qu’ils respectent l’image de marque.
 Organiser les fichiers et s’assurer que les versions les plus récentes sont clairement identifiées.
 Soutenir la publication du bulletin hebdomadaire sur les ventes, y compris la coordination, l’édition, la mise en page et la validation des soumissions.
 Tenir à jour le contenu SharePoint, en veillant à ce qu’il soit bien organisé, et assurer l’exactitude des dossiers de formation.
 Gérer les échéances concurrentes, communiquer l’état d’avancement des travaux, soulever les problèmes dès leur apparition et rechercher des tâches supplémentaires une fois que les priorités sont sur la bonne voie.
 Critères de sélection 
 Citoyenneté canadienne ou résidence permanente au Canada
 Étudiante ou étudiant qui suit actuellement un programme de premier cycle ou de maîtrise, ou qui a obtenu son diplôme au cours de la dernière année, dans un domaine pertinent :
 Administration des affaires
 Marketing
 Ressources humaines
 Commerce
 Commerce international
 Maîtrise des deux langues officielles 
 Atouts 
 Expérience de travail ou participation à un programme d’alternance travail-études dans un domaine connexe
 Sens aigu de l’éthique professionnelle, sens de l’initiative, bon jugement et capacité fiable à mener à bien les tâches confiées
 Capacité à travailler efficacement, tant de façon autonome qu’en équipe
 Capacité à utiliser Microsoft 365; expérience avec Canva ou Adobe (atout supplémentaire)
 Expérience dans le secteur des services financiers ou au sein d’une société d’État fédérale
 Avantages apportés par cette expérience 
 Expérience dans les domaines de la facilitation des ventes, de la formation, de la communication interne et du changement organisationnel
 Expérience de collaboration avec des experts en la matière et des partenaires au sein d’EDC
 Occasions d’acquérir des compétences pratiques en matière d’élaboration de contenu, de coordination des parties prenantes et de collaboration numérique
 Encadrement et commentaires de la part de professionnels de la facilitation chevronnés
 Compréhension de la traduction des priorités d’affaires en communications, en occasions d’apprentissage et en outils destinés au personnel de première ligne
 Offre d’emploi pour les personnes étudiantes et nouvellement diplômées : Nos offres d’emploi pour les personnes étudiantes et nouvellement diplômées comprennent des stages et des programmes d’alternance travail-études, tous conçus pour donner un bon départ à votre carrière. Un stage supplémentaire de quatre mois ou plus peut s’ajouter au stage d’automne de quatre mois, selon les besoins opérationnels. Le travail est normalement effectué à temps plein, mais il existe une certaine flexibilité en matière de travail à temps partiel.
 Notre programme est idéal pour les étudiantes et les étudiants et pour les professionnelles et les professionnels en début de carrière qui sont nouvellement diplômés et ont terminé leurs cours l’année dernière. Les stages effectués dans le cadre de notre programme peuvent faire partie d’un programme coopératif (COOP) universitaire accrédité.
 Aperçu d’un stage étudiant à EDC : 
 C’est l’occasion de tisser des relations avec des collègues provenant de secteurs divers et variés, mais aussi de déceler et de concrétiser des occasions d’amélioration et d’innovation. C’est apprendre et se perfectionner auprès des membres de la Société en profitant d’un programme d’encadrement et de mentorat. C’est évoluer dans un environnement ultraproductif, souple et dynamique et misant sur les technologies depuis nos carrefours communautaires des quatre coins du Canada.

 Vous recevrez un avis lorsque nous aurons reçu votre demande.

 HUNGRY is revolutionizing workplace dining with an unwavering commitment to obsessive hospitality and flawless execution. Founded in 2016 by entrepreneurs Eman Pahlavani and Jeff Grass, HUNGRY connects corporate offices in over 30 cities across the United States and Canada with top-tier chefs and local restaurants to deliver extraordinary culinary experiences. From large-format catering and memorable events to individually packaged group meals, snacks, and pantry solutions, HUNGRY ensures every detail is thoughtfully handled to prioritize quality and convenience. Rooted in a mission of social responsibility, HUNGRY fosters local economic growth while embracing eco-friendly practices — donating one meal for every two purchased, with more than 3 million meals donated to date.

 As a Food Partner Manager at Hungry, you'll own the success of our current partner network. You'll keep menus accurate, guide new partners through onboarding and getting set up with Hungry, and be the day-to-day point of contact restaurants and chefs count on. You'll track how specific items and menus are performing with our clients and turn that into real-time feedback partners can actually use, then work directly with the restaurant or chef to make adjustments that grow their sales.

 Food partner relationship management, and retention

 Assist Tech Team with creating and designing enhancements and improvements to the website or vendor dashboard
 Support in any day to day incidents and issues; acting as the main point of contact for our Food Partner network and collaborating with our Sales, Operations, CS teams 
 Build brand recognition and credibility with our Food Partner network
 Minimum of 2+ years of catering sales experience or food partner management experience in a high-volume environment
 Food knowledge required to create menus in collaboration with the chefs in your market
 Demonstrated customer relations experience including direct outreach to establish business
 Be able to oversee multiple accounts simultaneously
 Experience creating menus for various catering needs and knowledge of portioning and dietary restrictions 
 Tremendous attention to detail 
 Opportunistic drive and tenacity 
 Excellent organizational techniques 
 Excellent oral and written communication skills 
 Poised and personable presentation techniques
 Positive and proactive attitude

 Ingénieur(e) principal(e) en conception de circuits RF et analogiques 
 Relevant du directeur de l’ingénierie optique, l’ingénieur(e) principal(e) en conception RF/analogique se joindra à une équipe multidisciplinaire de R-D qui développe des composants photoniques haute vitesse destinés à des produits de communications optiques avancées. Dans ce rôle, la personne fournira une expertise approfondie en ingénierie RF/micro-ondes pour la conception, la simulation, la caractérisation et l’optimisation de composants optoélectroniques haute vitesse et des structures RF connexes. Elle mettra à profit son expertise en électromagnétisme, en circuits micro-ondes et en techniques de mesure afin de résoudre des défis techniques complexes et de contribuer au développement de technologies photoniques de prochaine génération.
 Votre contribution 
 Concevoir, simuler et analyser des structures RF/micro-ondes, notamment des lignes de transmission, des interconnexions et des structures passives sur des plateformes de circuits imprimés (PCB), hybrides et de circuits intégrés.
 Mettre à profit des connaissances approfondies en électromagnétisme, en théorie des lignes de transmission, en circuits et en techniques de mesure pour les composants optoélectroniques haute vitesse et les applications de boîtiers connexes.
 Effectuer et orienter la caractérisation RF/micro-ondes et électro-optique de dispositifs photoniques et passifs à haute fréquence.
 Utiliser des outils de simulation de circuits et de simulation électromagnétique par éléments finis pour modéliser, analyser et optimiser les conceptions RF/micro-ondes.
 Analyser les données de mesure et de simulation, cerner les limitations de performance et recommander des améliorations de conception.
 Collaborer avec des spécialistes en ingénierie optique, photonique, électrique, mécanique, en boîtiers et dans d’autres disciplines afin de résoudre des défis de conception complexes.
 Participer aux revues techniques et aux revues de conception, et mettre son expertise en ingénierie à contribution tout au long du cycle de développement.
 Fournir des conseils techniques et partager son expertise en RF/micro-ondes avec les autres membres de l’équipe d’ingénierie.
 Exigences essentielles 
 Baccalauréat ou études supérieures en génie électrique, en physique appliquée ou dans une discipline technique connexe.
 Solide expérience professionnelle en ingénierie RF/micro-ondes, en conception haute fréquence ou dans un domaine étroitement lié.
 Solide compréhension de l’électromagnétisme, des lignes de transmission, des circuits haute fréquence, des signaux et systèmes ainsi que des techniques de mesure.
 Expérience en conception et en analyse de structures et d’interconnexions RF/micro-ondes.
 Expérience avec les outils de simulation RF/micro-ondes et de modélisation électromagnétique.
 Bonne compréhension pratique des mesures à haute fréquence, de la caractérisation, de l’étalonnage et de l’analyse de données expérimentales.
 Solides compétences en analyse et en résolution de problèmes, avec la capacité de résoudre des problèmes d’ingénierie multidisciplinaires complexes.
 Capacité à communiquer clairement des concepts techniques et à collaborer efficacement dans un environnement de R-D.
 Atouts 
 Expérience avec Ansys HFSS, Keysight ADS ou des outils comparables de simulation RF/électromagnétique.
 Expérience avec des dispositifs optoélectroniques haute vitesse, tels que des modulateurs ou des photodétecteurs.
 Connaissance des amplificateurs haute fréquence et des amplificateurs transimpédance.
 Expérience avec les analyseurs de réseaux vectoriels et les techniques de caractérisation RF.
 Compréhension de la modulation numérique et des technologies de communications optiques.
 Expérience avec des composants photoniques ou des produits de communications optiques.

Group Ventures is Valsoft's incubator. We find opportunities in the market and build companies to address them. The finance team inside Group Ventures keeps the books for four of those companies so far: ValPay, Tenerum, Sadie Technology, and Plug & Pay.
 We're looking for a financial analyst to run their day-to-day accounting cycle: vendors, payments, banking operations, recurring schedules, and close support. You'll work directly with the Finance Controller, who keeps responsibility for accounting judgement, financial statements, and technical positions. You'll be the one running the accounting engine each day.
 The work spans several entities and seven currencies (CAD, USD, EUR, GBP, AUD, NZD, CHF) on NetSuite OneWorld. Volume is high and close deadlines are tight.
 AI should be part of how you work. Use it to draft, analyse, and automate the repetitive parts of the cycle. You're responsible for the accuracy of whatever gets posted.
 What we value 
 Accuracy, and the habit of checking your own work before anyone else has to.
 Finishing what you own without being chased.
 Understanding how each entity earns and spends money.
 Discretion with confidential financial information.
 Curiosity, and a willingness to fix a process that keeps producing the same error.
 The honesty to say when something is wrong, including your own work.
 What you'll do 
 Keep payables accurate and vendors paid on time
 Monitor the AP shared mailboxes (ValPay, Tenerum, Sadie) and run the weekly invoice-entry batch: triage, rename and file PDFs, code invoices by entity, division and GL account, prepare the NetSuite bill import file, and attach supporting documents. Process recurring invoices per established coding rules.
 Obtain missing spend approvals from budget owners, reconcile vendor statements, investigate differences, and clear past-due invoices.
 Set up and maintain vendor records in NetSuite, including banking details, tax forms and payment terms, checking every banking change before it goes in.
 Prepare the weekly payment run: payment proposal, draft-only payment entry in the banking portal, remittance advices, and approval follow-up.
 Keep cash and bank records reconciled
 Download bank statements and transactions for all entities, code and post entries in NetSuite, and prepare the monthly bank reconciliations with reconciling items listed for review.
 Own the credit card cycle: collect receipts, chase cardholders, produce the monthly expense file, and prepare the reconciliation and journal-entry upload file.
 Get customers invoiced and cash applied
 Issue and send customer invoices, and follow up on missing or corrected ones.
 Apply cash receipts, maintain the AR aging, and handle first-level collection follow-up, flagging past-due accounts and disputes to the Controller for escalation.
 Support the month-end close
 Maintain recurring schedules (prepaids, accruals, fixed assets and depreciation, deferred revenue) and prepare balance sheet reconciliations for lower-complexity accounts, documenting open items.
 Prepare standard and recurring journal entries with full supporting documentation for Controller review and approval, then upload the approved files to NetSuite and verify posting accuracy.
 Run intercompany confirmations: prepare balance confirmations, circulate them to group entities, follow up, and assemble settlement support.
 Keep records audit-ready and support the Controller
 File and archive supporting documentation per the established folder structure, pull samples and documents requested by external auditors, and keep audit folders current.
 Handle finance requests in Jira, gathering documentation, keeping tickets updated and closing them once resolved. Write and maintain the procedures for the tasks you own.
 Work with the Controller on ad hoc requests and special projects: onboarding new entities or acquisitions, opening and closing bank accounts, system implementations, and data gathering for analyses and reporting. Prepare the documents, data extracts and working files for files the Controller leads, and pick up other accounting-cycle work as team needs and period priorities change.
 What you'll bring 
 A DEC in accounting and management techniques, an AEC in accounting, or equivalent training.
 Two to four years of full-cycle accounting experience.
 Intermediate to advanced Excel. You're comfortable with lookups, pivot tables, and high volumes of data.
 ERP experience. NetSuite is strongly preferred; Sage, Dynamics, or QuickBooks are accepted.
 Accuracy and attention to detail, with the discipline to meet tight close deadlines.
 Self-direction and organisation. You can carry a high volume of recurring tasks with minimal supervision.
 Follow-through. You chase the missing approval, receipt, or confirmation until it arrives.
 Discretion and judgement with confidential financial information.
 Clear writing. You can explain a reconciling item or a vendor discrepancy in a few lines.
 You use AI tools in your work and check the results before they reach the ledger.
 Useful experience 
 Multi-entity or multi-currency accounting.
 Power Query.
 Payments, fintech, or software.
 Using a corporate banking portal.
 Jira.
 Writing procedures for a finance team that is still being built.
 Who will enjoy this role 
 You notice when a vendor statement doesn't match, a bank line has no home, or an intercompany balance is off by the same amount two months running. You want to know why, and you fix the cause.
 In one week you might clear an invoice batch across three entities, chase a cardholder for receipts, reconcile an AUD bank account, and pull audit samples. Most of the work recurs, and the value is in getting it right every time.
 The hard parts are specific. Volume is high and the close date doesn't move. Across seven currencies and several entities, small mistakes compound. You prepare and the Controller decides: accounting judgement and final approvals sit with someone else. Processes are being built as the team grows, so sometimes you'll do a task that has no procedure yet, then write one.
 Why this role matters 
 Group Ventures builds companies for Valsoft, and its growth has been recognized on Deloitte's Technology Fast 50. ValPay operates as a payment facilitator, so other businesses can accept payments without building their own merchant infrastructure. Sadie builds AI voice technology for restaurants and hospitality, with customers in Australia, Europe, the United States, and Canada.
 Each new company the group builds becomes another entity in the finance team's books, with its own bank accounts, vendors, and close. The team is small and still being built out. This hire takes on the day-to-day accounting cycle so the Controller can focus on accounting judgement, financial statements, and technical positions. You'll see how a multi-entity, multi-currency technology group runs from the inside, and as the team scales there is room to take on more analytical work.

 Flexible time off policy

ABOUT US

Sierra is the leading platform for customer-facing AI agents, working with many of the world's biggest brands — including The GAP, Rocket Mortgage, SoFi, Sutter Health, and SoftBank — to transform how they serve customers and grow their businesses. We are primarily an in-person company based in San Francisco, with growing offices across North America, Europe, and Asia.

We are guided by a set of values that are at the core of our actions and define our culture: Trust, Customer Obsession, Craftsmanship, Intensity, and a commitment to balancing Family along the way. These values are the foundation of our work, and we are committed to upholding them in everything we do.

Our co-founders are Bret Taylor https://www.linkedin.com/in/brettaylor/ and Clay Bavor https://www.linkedin.com/in/claybavor/. Bret currently serves as Board Chair of OpenAI. Previously, he was co-CEO of Salesforce (which had acquired the company he founded, Quip) and CTO of Facebook. Bret was also one of Google's earliest product managers and co-creator of Google Maps. Before founding Sierra, Clay spent 18 years at Google, where he most recently led Google Labs. Earlier, he started and led Google’s AR/VR effort, Project Starline, and Google Lens. Before that, Clay led the product and design teams for Google Workspace.


WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Design and deliver production-grade AI agents https://sierra.ai/blog/meet-the-ai-agent-engineer: You'll build and ship highly performant, reliable, and intuitive AI agents that are central, mission-critical and drive revenue directly to Sierra's growth. These aren't prototypes—they are powerful, scalable systems running in production environments across industries like finance, healthcare, and commerce.

 - Drive the Agent Development Life Cycle https://sierra.ai/blog/agent-development-life-cycle (ADLC): You'll have complete ownership and autonomy from initial pilot through deployment and continuous iteration. You'll be responsible for building, tuning, and evolving AI agents in production environments, defining the standard for ADLC best practices along the way.

 - Partner with large enterprises and cutting-edge startups: You’ll work directly with leaders at some of the world’s largest enterprises to understand their most pressing business challenges, and build AI agents that transform how they operate at scale. You'll also partner with the most cutting-edge startups in Silicon Valley, embedding AI agents across their entire business stack to drive innovation and efficiency.

 - Build the future of the platform: Your direct work with customers will guide the evolution of Sierra's core platform. You'll surface unmet needs, prototype new tools and features, and collaborate with research, product, and platform to shape the future of AI agent development and Sierra's product.


EXAMPLE PROJECTS

These are some examples of projects that engineers on our team have worked on recently:

 - Design and build AI agents for large telecommunications and media companies that consistently outperform human agents in managing subscription churn

 - Develop and refine AI agents capable of navigating complex customer interactions, like troubleshooting a broken device and personalizing product recommendations

 - Create generalizable AI agent frameworks tailored for industry-specific use cases. See some examples in our financial services blog https://sierra.ai/blog/five-ways-to-use-ai-agents-financial-services!

 - Facilitate design partnerships for new product initiatives, such as new agent architectures, self-service capabilities, and generative agent development

 - Experiment with the latest voice models and figure out how to integrate them at scale to enterprise-grade customers


WHAT YOU'LL BRING

 - Experience building and scaling end-to-end production systems

 - Strong technical problem-solving skills, especially in fast-changing, ambiguous environments

 - A builder and tinkerer’s mindset with high agency - you find creative ways to overcome obstacles and ship

 - Comfort working directly with customers to understand their needs and solve real-world problems

 - Excellent communication skills - clear, direct, and persuasive across technical and non-technical audiences


EVEN BETTER...

 - Experience building or deploying AI/LLM systems in production

 - Have been a founder or founding engineer - you know what it means to balance craft, ownership, and speed

 - Familiarity with tools that power today's AI agents: eval frameworks, agent tooling, RAG pipelines, and prompt engineering

 - Prior experience with React, TypeScript, and/or Go

 - Previous roles where you interfaced with customers or led technical projects with external stakeholders


OUR VALUES

 - Trust: We build trust with our customers with our accountability, empathy, quality, and responsiveness. We build trust in AI by making it more accessible, safe, and useful. We build trust with each other by showing up for each other professionally and personally, creating an environment that enables all of us to do our best work.

 - Customer Obsession: We deeply understand our customers’ business goals and relentlessly focus on driving outcomes, not just technical milestones. Everyone at the company knows and spends time with our customers. When our customer is having an issue, we drop everything and fix it.

 - Craftsmanship: We get the details right, from the words on the page to the system architecture. We have good taste. When we notice something isn’t right, we take the time to fix it. We are proud of the products we produce. We continuously self-reflect to continuously self-improve.

 - Intensity: We know we don’t have the luxury of patience. We play to win. We care about our product being the best, and when it isn’t, we fix it. When we fail, we talk about it openly and without blame so we succeed the next time.

 - Family: We know that balance and intensity are compatible, and we model it in our actions and processes. We are the best technology company for parents. We support and respect each other and celebrate each other’s personal and professional achievements.


WHAT WE OFFER

We want our benefits to reflect our values and offer the following to full-time employees:

 - Flexible (unlimited) paid time off

 - Medical, dental, and vision benefits for you and your family

 - Life insurance and disability benefits

 - Retirement plan dependent on country of employment

 - Parental leave

 - Fertility and family building benefits through Carrot

 - Lunch, as well as delicious snacks and coffee to keep you energized 

 - Discretionary benefit stipend giving people the ability to spend where it matters most

Eligible full-time employees can participate in Sierra's equity plans subject to the terms of the applicable plans and policies.

About us 
 At NATIONAL, we are driven by purpose, creativity, and connection. For 50 years, our teams across Canada have been delivering strategic communications expertise that helps organizations shape conversations that matter.
 NATIONAL is seeking a senior communications leader for Newfoundland and Labrador. While this opportunity is currently posted at the Director level, we welcome interest from experienced communications professionals and seasoned executives, with level, scope, and title to be considered based on experience, capability, and market presence.
 This is a rare opportunity for someone who knows the province, understands how decisions are made, and can move confidently between public affairs, government relations, corporate communications, and marketing conversations.
 Our Newfoundland and Labrador presence is an important part of our Atlantic and national network. We work with clients across sectors, regions, and issues, helping them navigate complex environments, build trust, and communicate with clarity. With a strong local and regional foundation and access to the full strength of NATIONAL’s offices across Canada, this role offers the opportunity to help shape what comes next in one of the country’s most distinctive and strategically important markets.
 The role 
 This is a hands-on, senior market-building opportunity for someone who wants to be both strategic and practical, visible and grounded, independent and deeply connected to a national team. We are looking for an entrepreneurial leader who can help grow NATIONAL’s presence in Newfoundland and Labrador while contributing to client work across Atlantic Canada and the broader NATIONAL network. Whether you’re currently living in the region, or looking to return home, the ideal candidate is deeply connected to the province. They understand the local business, political, and community landscape, and they bring the judgment, presence, and credibility to advise executives, engage stakeholders, and represent NATIONAL in the market.
 Our office is located within the Board of Trade in St. John’s, offering a strong connection to the local business community and an energizing space for client work, collaboration, and growth.
 What you will do 
 As a key member of the Atlantic and Canadian Advisory and Public Affairs practice team, you will provide senior counsel to clients navigating complex communications, public affairs, and reputational challenges. Our roster of clients are closely connected to the biggest opportunities and challenges NL is facing. You will bring a strong understanding of government, business, community, and media environments in Newfoundland and Labrador, with particular interest in sectors such as energy, defense, economic development, healthcare and other areas shaping the future of the province. Ideally, your experience and skillset can contribute to client needs outside of NL and outside of Atlantic Canada.
 You will help lead and grow client relationships, identify new opportunities, and connect clients with the right expertise from across NATIONAL. You will be expected to work independently, think strategically, and manage mandates with confidence, while also knowing when and how to bring in colleagues from other offices and practice areas.
 You will represent NATIONAL in the Newfoundland and Labrador market, helping to strengthen our visibility, relationships, and reputation. You will be comfortable in a boardroom, at a community event, in a government relations discussion, or in a marketing strategy conversation. You do not need to be a specialist in every discipline, but you should be an integrated thinker who understands how public affairs, communications, marketing, stakeholder engagement, and reputation intersect. In this role, you will be part of the broader.
 What you bring 
 You are someone excited about local and regional connectivity and are a trusted advisor with strong judgment, sound instincts, and the ability to build relationships across sectors. You are self-motivated and credible with executives, comfortable with elected officials and senior public servants, and able to speak naturally with people from a wide range of backgrounds and perspectives.
 You likely bring:
 Senior experience in public affairs, government relations, strategic communications, crisis communications, public relations, or a related professional services environment
 Strong knowledge of Newfoundland and Labrador’s political, business, community, and media landscape
 Experience or strong familiarity with sectors such as energy, defense, infrastructure, natural resources, economic development, or other regulated or high-profile industries
 The ability to lead client relationships, provide wise counsel, and manage complex mandates with limited day-to-day oversight
 A practical understanding of marketing and integrated communications, with the ability to contribute meaningfully to broader brand, reputation, and campaign conversations
 Strong writing, presentation, facilitation, and relationship-building skills
 An entrepreneurial mindset and interest in helping grow NATIONAL’s presence in Newfoundland and Labrador
 The ability to collaborate across offices, especially with Atlantic Canada, Ottawa, and other teams across the NATIONAL network
 A degree or equivalent experience in communications, public relations, political science, business, public policy, journalism, marketing, or a related field
 How you work 
 You are strategic, but not removed from the work. You can see the larger picture, identify what matters, and turn advice into action. You are calm under pressure, clear in your counsel, and comfortable working in situations where the path forward is not always obvious. You have good judgement.
 You build trust easily. You are good in a room, thoughtful in your approach, and able to move between senior executives, community leaders, public officials, colleagues, and clients with confidence and respect. You are a good writer and easily adjust to different mediums and audiences. You are collaborative, but highly self-sufficient. You can build something without needing a large local team around you, and you know how to draw on the strength of a national network when clients would benefit from additional expertise.
 You are values-driven, discreet, adaptable, and committed to excellent client service.
 What we offer 
 The opportunity to help shape NATIONAL’s value as a consultancy in Newfoundland and Labrador
 A senior, market-facing role with room to grow based on experience, capability, and ambition
 A connected national platform with strong Atlantic Canadian collaboration
 Exposure to meaningful client work across public affairs, government relations, corporate communications, marketing, and reputation
 A dynamic, entrepreneurial environment with the support of one of Canada’s most respected communications consultancies
 Competitive compensation, commensurate with level and experience
 Hybrid flexibility with an expectation of meaningful presence in the St. John’s market
 A commitment to diversity, equity, and inclusion in all that we do
 How to apply 
 Qualified candidates are invited to apply by submitting a resume and a brief cover letter outlining their interest in the role, connection to Newfoundland and Labrador, and relevant experience.
 NATIONAL is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. Should you require accommodation during the selection process, please inform us.
 Please note that only candidates selected for further consideration will be contacted. As part of our recruitment process, we use artificial intelligence tools to assist with the screening, assessment, and selection of applicants for this role. Thank you for considering a career with NATIONAL.
 NATIONAL Public Relations provides creative communications solutions that move people in thought and actions. We bring together a team of 300 seasoned professionals, who are committed to helping organizations of all sizes and in all sectors understand their challenges and opportunities and solve the issues they are facing. For 47 years, NATIONAL has been at the center of issues and industries that matter, leading change for today and tomorrow.
 NATIONAL is Canada’s leading public relations firm, with offices in Vancouver, Calgary, Toronto, Ottawa, Montreal, Quebec City, Saint John, Halifax and St. John’s. Its network includes Time & Space, a leader in media strategy, data analysis, planning and execution.
 NATIONAL Public Relations is an AVENIR GLOBAL company, the largest Canadian-owned global communications firm, ranked among the 25 largest in the world with offices in 23 locations across Canada, the U.S., Europe and the Middle East. For more information about NATIONAL, please visit our website or follow us on LinkedIn and X .

 À propos de Pratt & Whitney Canada 
 Pratt & Whitney Canada (P&WC) est un leader mondial de l’innovation aérospatiale, dont le siège social est situé à Longueuil, au Québec, depuis 1928.  Depuis près de 100 ans, nos équipes sont à l’avant-garde des technologies de propulsion, repoussant les limites afin de rendre nos moteurs plus performants et fiables. Nos moteurs soutiennent des missions essentielles, du transport de passagers et de marchandises aux services médicaux d’urgence, aux opérations humanitaires et à la lutte contre les feux de forêt, partout dans le monde.

 Stratégie d’architecture pour le Canada et mise en œuvre de l’IA

 Établir les feuilles de route fondamentales: Concevoir et mettre en œuvre une stratégie infonuagique et une stratégie de données complètes, adaptées aux besoins de nos activités canadiennes, afin de mettre les bases de la mise en œuvre d’une stratégie d’IA à l’échelle de l’entreprise.

 You’ll take ownership of accounting and finance work across a portfolio of growing companies. That means getting into the details when you need to, but also understanding the bigger picture and what your clients actually need.
 You’ll work directly with founders, senior finance professionals and international clients , helping them keep their finances moving and solving problems as they come up.
 One client might need help getting their month-end close under control. Another might have a reporting issue, a tax question or something that doesn’t quite make sense in the books. You’ll need to be comfortable figuring things out, asking questions and getting to the answer. 
 This is a hands-on role in a fast-moving firm. You’ll have support from experienced finance professionals, but we expect you to take ownership of your work and keep things moving without waiting to be told what to do. 
 What You’ll Do
 You’ll take ownership of:
 Full-cycle accounting for a portfolio of technology and startup clients 
 Preparing and reviewing financial statements and management reporting 
 Reconciliations and month-end and year-end close 
 Supporting corporate and personal tax preparation and planning 
 Supporting audit, review and compilation engagements 
 Working directly with clients to answer questions and resolve accounting issues 
 Keeping client deliverables moving and communicating when something needs attention 
 Looking for ways to improve processes and build better, more scalable ways of working 
 Supporting junior team members and working closely with our senior finance team
 What We’re Looking For
 You have a Bachelor’s degree in Accounting or a related field and 4+ years of relevant accounting experience , including strong full-cycle accounting experience.
 You’re comfortable with financial reporting, reconciliations and month-end close, and you know how to manage several clients and deadlines without losing track of the details.
 You’re also comfortable working directly with clients. Strong English communication skills are important , because you’ll be explaining financial information, asking questions and working through problems with people at different levels of an organization.
 Most importantly, you’re someone who takes ownership . If something doesn’t look right, you investigate it. If you see a problem, you don’t just point it out. You help solve it. And if there’s a better way of doing something, we want you to say it.
 Experience with public accounting, audit, tax, Taxprep, CaseWare, QuickBooks Online or Xero is a plus.
 Experience working with technology, SaaS, fintech, Web3 or digital assets is also a plus.
 A CPA designation is preferred.
 Why Convoy?
 You’ll work with interesting companies, smart people and problems that don’t always come with an instruction manual. 
 You’ll have direct exposure to founders and senior finance leaders and get to see how growing companies actually operate. Because we’re a small team, your work is visible and your contribution matters. 
 You’ll be based in Toronto alongside most of the team, but our clients and colleagues aren’t all in one place. You’ll get exposure to different businesses, industries and markets , without being stuck doing the same thing every day.
 We also make time for team lunches, happy hours and, when the numbers are good, the occasional team trip.
 It’s fast-paced. It’s challenging. And it’s definitely not boring. 
 If you want to keep learning, take real ownership and grow beyond traditional accounting , we’d like to hear from you.
 Compensation
 CAD 70,000–90,000 per year , depending on experience and qualifications.
 How to Apply
 Send us your resume and a brief overview of your experience.
 We’d love to hear from you.

Role Overview:

Advance the state of the art for model post training, ship state of the art models to production, and bridge the gap between research and production.
